problem.title: One platform for the whole business
paragraphs: The platform runs the daily business of several group companies, each on its own instance: customers, tickets, offers, orders, invoicing, projects, time tracking and reporting. It is a long-lived Yii application, so the work is as much about modernising what exists as about building what is new.

I have developed and maintained it since 2024, first part-time and now full-time with a wider scope: bringing AI into the platform and building new modules. The code is private, so this page describes the work without screenshots.

items.title: Streaming Ad Platform
items.description: Ad platform for a streaming service, built with Node.js, TypeScript and React: ad decisions for video players, real-time campaign analytics, prepaid billing with EU VAT, and a dashboard in English and German.
features: Ad Decisions & VAST for Video Players

study.tagline: An ad platform for a streaming service: it picks the ad for every ad break, counts every view exactly once, and bills what was delivered.

numbers.label: events per second in the load test, none lost or counted twice
for a 90-day report over 9.9 million rows
to count a campaign's unique viewers for a day
from a Redis outage to the alert email

problem.title: Three parties, one ad break
paragraphs: Streaming services with an ad tier show short ads before, during and after episodes. The advertiser wants the ad seen by the right people for a set budget. The platform has to choose an ad for every break and keep each campaign on schedule. The viewer watches, and the player reports what happened.

I built the part in the middle, end to end: campaigns and teams, the ad decision, a real video player, event counting, analytics, billing and the operations around it. All brands, shows and traffic in the demo are fictional.

built.title: Ad decisions
built.text: For each ad break the platform keeps the campaigns that match the dates, schedule, limits, country, device, slot, genre and audience. Guaranteed campaigns that are behind go first, and the rest is sold in a second-price auction. Any VAST 4.2 player can ask for an ad.

built.title: From upload to playback
built.text: A manager uploads a video, FFmpeg converts it in the background, an admin approves it, and the demo streaming site plays it before, during and after an episode.

built.title: Analytics and reports
built.text: Live charts, reach and frequency, drop-off, A/B tests that only name a winner at 95% confidence, and saved reports emailed as CSV and PDF.

built.title: Prepaid billing
built.text: A ledger that is never edited, holds for running budgets, invoices numbered with no gaps, EU VAT with VIES checks, currencies at the European Central Bank's daily rate and optional Stripe Checkout.

built.title: AI assistant
built.text: Optional and off by default. It answers questions such as why a campaign is behind, using read-only tools, and suggests changes that only apply once a person approves them. It runs on a free local model or a paid API.

built.title: Operations
built.text: Structured logs, metrics, traces and alerts in Grafana, and daily backups that are restored into a scratch database to prove they work.

flow.title: How an event is counted

lanes.title: Player
items: Reports each event with a unique ID

lanes.title: API
items: A Redis script drops IDs already seen
Queues the rest in the same atomic step

lanes.title: Worker
items: Saves the totals and the queue entry's ID together

flow.note: A retry can't count twice, and a crash can't lose or repeat an event.

hard.title: Limits that hold when requests race
hard.text: Budgets, goals and frequency caps are reserved in the same atomic Redis step that picks the ad, not checked afterwards. A campaign can't pass its goal, however many requests arrive at once.

hard.title: Counting exactly once
hard.text: An entry stays on the queue until its totals are saved, and its ID is saved in the same transaction. The load test included a worker crash, and no event was lost or counted twice.

hard.title: Fast reports without a data warehouse
hard.text: Events are added into one row per campaign, hour, show, slot, country and device, so the table grows with variety, not with traffic. Unique viewers are counted in HyperLogLog sketches.

items.title: CareerCraft
items.description: AI-assisted job search platform for the German market, built with Laravel 13 and Livewire 4: one structured career profile becomes several CVs, with CV import by a local AI model, saved PDF and Word versions, and a check of how applicant tracking systems read each one.

study.tagline: A job search platform for the German market: one career profile becomes every CV, and each version is checked the way an applicant tracking system reads it.

numbers.label: CV templates, one of them the German tabular Lebenslauf
AI providers to choose from, one free and local
languages on every screen and in every email
CV files kept after an import

problem.title: One career, many applications
paragraphs: Applying for jobs means rewriting the same career into a slightly different CV each time, and never being sure what an employer's software makes of the PDF. In Germany there is a second format to maintain as well: the tabular Lebenslauf with photo, place, date and signature.

CareerCraft keeps one structured career profile and builds every CV from it. It is in development: the foundation, accounts, the profile, CV import, the CV builder and the AI layer are built. Cover letters, job matching and application tracking come next.

built.title: Career profile
built.text: Experience with achievements, education, skills with levels, projects, certificates and languages at CEFR levels, with a strength score that lists what to add next.

built.title: Import
built.text: Upload a PDF or Word CV and a local AI model suggests what goes where, or upload LinkedIn's data export, which is read without AI. The person checks every field before anything is saved.

built.title: CV builder
built.text: Several CVs from one profile, four templates, a live A4 preview that shows where pages end, and headings and dates that follow the CV's language.

built.title: Saved versions
built.text: Each version keeps its PDF and Word file exactly as they were, so it is always clear what was sent. Any two versions can be compared line by line.

built.title: Parser check
built.text: Every PDF is read back as plain text, the way an applicant tracking system reads it, and anything that doesn't come through as whole words is listed.

built.title: AI layer
built.text: An admin picks Ollama, Claude or any OpenAI-compatible API, and sets a daily allowance per person and token prices. Every request is recorded with its tokens and cost.

flow.title: From profile to a sent CV

lanes.title: Profile
items: Imported from a CV or LinkedIn

lanes.title: Gotenberg
items: Renders the same page as the preview
PDF and Word file saved as a version

lanes.title: Parser check
items: Reads the PDF back as text
Lists what a parser would miss

flow.note: The PDF is made from the same page as the preview, so what you see is what is sent.

hard.title: An AI that only copies facts
hard.text: The CV reader is told to copy what the CV says, never to add an employer, date or skill, and to ignore instructions written inside the CV. Its output is a suggestion: the person ticks what to keep.

hard.title: One layer for every AI feature
hard.text: All requests go through one runner that retries an overloaded provider, streams answers, stops at the daily allowance and records usage. Keys for paid providers stay in the environment and are never stored in the database.

hard.title: PDFs a parser can read
hard.text: The templates are single-column with plain text in reading order. The parser check proves that for each version instead of assuming it.
